objective_for_doctor: A 45-year-old Male patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: I have right posterior chest wall pain, a cough, and sensitive pain.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Hi doctor. I’ve been having pain in my right back/chest wall area, and I also have a cough. The pain feels very sensitive, and it’s about a 6 out of 10. I’ve also had chronic tiredness and some unintentional weight loss.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—does your cough produce any mucus or blood, and do you have fever or shortness of breath?  
Doctor: Is the chest wall pain worse with deep breathing or movement, and have you noticed any skin rash or new blisters in that same right-sided area?  
Doctor: Given your weight loss and chronic fatigue, I’m concerned—can you tell me how long this has been going on and whether you smoke or have known exposures (TB, asbestos, recent sick contacts)?

My cough sometimes brings mucus, but I don’t have blood in it. I don’t know about fever, and I’m not feeling short of breath.  

The chest wall pain gets worse when I take deep breaths and when I move. I haven’t noticed any rash or new blisters on that area.  

This has been going on for a while—long enough that I’ve had chronic fatigue and lost weight without trying. I do smoke cigarettes, and I’m around secondhand smoke every day, but I haven’t had recent international travel. I don’t know of any TB exposure, asbestos, or sick contacts.

Doctor: I need to clarify a few things—do you feel any night sweats, and have you had any loss of appetite or swollen neck/armpit lymph nodes? Also, is the pain sharply localized to one spot on the right ribs where I can reproduce it by pressing?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray (PA & lateral)  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_diff + CMP + CRP/ESR

I haven’t noticed night sweats. My appetite is not great because of the weight loss, but I can’t say for sure—no swollen neck or armpit lumps that I’ve noticed.  

Yes, the pain is sharply in one spot on the right ribs, and I can reproduce it when I press on it.

Doctor: Thanks—sharp, reproducible focal rib tenderness plus pleuritic/movement-related pain often points to a chest wall cause (like costochondral injury or rib fracture), but your weight loss and smoking also raise concern for malignancy or infection; we’ll still rule out serious causes.  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray (PA & lateral); REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_diff + CMP + CRP/ESR.  
Doctor: Quick next—any recent trauma/heavy lifting, and how long has the weight loss been going on (weeks vs months)?

No recent trauma or heavy lifting that I can think of.  

The weight loss has been going on for months, not just a few weeks.

Doctor: Given no trauma and reproducible focal rib tenderness, chest wall pathology (e.g., intercostal muscle strain or costochondritis) is likely, but months-long weight loss in a smoker means we must exclude malignancy or TB—can you confirm if the cough is persistent and how many pounds you’ve lost?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest_with_contrast (or CT_Chest if contrast contraindicated)  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Sputum_AFB_smear_and_culture (x2–3) and consider Quantiferon_TB_Gold
Yes, the cough feels persistent. I don’t know the exact number of pounds I’ve lost, but it’s been unintentional over the last few months.

Doctor: I’m going to ask two quick questions: do you have any shortness of breath, and is the cough worse at night or when lying down? Also, have you noticed any change in the size/shape of the painful area (swelling or a “bump”)?  
Doctor: I’m also concerned enough with months-long weight loss in a smoker plus persistent cough that I need advanced imaging—REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest_with_contrast (or CT_Chest if contrast contraindicated).

I don’t have shortness of breath. I haven’t really noticed if the cough is worse at night or when I lie down.  

The painful area hasn’t changed much—no swelling or a bump that I’ve noticed.

Doctor: With pleuritic/movement-related **reproducible focal rib tenderness** and no rash/blisters, chest-wall pain is likely; however, months-long unintentional weight loss in a smoker with persistent cough means we must exclude **lung cancer and TB**, so I’m ordering: REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest_with_contrast (if renal function allows).  
Doctor: Also, do you have any **history of shingles** in the past (or severe burning pain in a stripe before the pain), and have you ever had a **recent normal** chest X-ray or any prior imaging?

I don’t think I’ve had shingles before, and I haven’t had a severe burning pain in a stripe beforehand.  

I don’t know of any recent normal chest X-ray, and I don’t have any prior imaging that I can recall.

Doctor: Given no prior shingles and no dermatomal “burning stripe” history, shingles is less likely, so the key remaining causes are musculoskeletal chest wall pain vs lung malignancy/TB despite focal tenderness—have you ever had recent fevers (even mild) or very dark/foamy sputum?  
Doctor: Also, I need to know your age at smoking start and roughly how many pack-years you’ve smoked (or just: how many cigarettes per day and for how many years)?

I haven’t had fevers that I know of, and I don’t have very dark or foamy sputum.  

I started smoking when I was about 20 years old, and I currently smoke about a pack a day for around 25 years.

Doctor: Thanks—your long smoking history (≈25 pack-years) plus persistent cough and months-long unintentional weight loss means we must urgently exclude lung cancer and TB, even though the pain is reproducible. I’m ordering: REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest_with_contrast + REQUEST TEST: Sputum_AFB_smear_and_culture (x2–3) + Quantiferon_TB_Gold + REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_diff + CMP + CRP/ESR.  

Doctor: While we wait, I want one final check: do you have any persistent hoarseness, new trouble swallowing, or coughing that’s progressively worsening?

I haven’t noticed persistent hoarseness or any trouble swallowing.  

As for the cough, it feels persistent but I can’t say it’s getting progressively worse.

Doctor: Given your 25 pack-years, persistent cough, and months-long unintentional weight loss—plus reproducible focal right rib tenderness—I need to exclude lung cancer and TB despite the chest-wall-like tenderness; I’m making the diagnosis based on clinical probability that this is **chest wall pain with high-risk lung pathology until proven otherwise**.  
DIAGNOSIS READY: Chest wall pain likely (costochondral/intercostal strain) — but rule out serious causes (lung cancer and pulmonary TB) urgently based on smoking + weight loss + persistent cough.
